summary: TCP opens a connection with a three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. It agrees initial sequence numbers and confirms that both sides can send and receive before any data flows.

sections.heading: The exchange (RFC 9293, section 3.5)
sections.body: Client calls connect(); server is in LISTEN. Example initial sequence numbers 100 (client) and 300 (server):
sections.code:
Client                          Server
CLOSED                          LISTEN
  --- SYN seq=100 ----------->  
SYN-SENT                        SYN-RECEIVED
  <-- SYN+ACK seq=300 ack=101 -- 
ESTABLISHED                     
  --- ACK seq=101 ack=301 ----->  
                                ESTABLISHED

sections.heading: Why three steps
sections.body: Each side must send a SYN and have it acknowledged. The server's SYN and its ACK of the client's SYN are combined into one packet (SYN+ACK), so four messages become three. Both directions are thereby synchronized.

sections.heading: What is negotiated
bullets: Initial sequence numbers (ISNs), one per direction.
Window scale factor, SACK-permitted, and timestamps options.

sections.heading: Initial sequence numbers
sections.body: ISNs must be unpredictable, otherwise an attacker can forge segments. RFC 9293 describes ISN = a 4-microsecond clock + a keyed hash of the connection 4-tuple and a secret that outsiders cannot compute.

sections.heading: SYN consumes a sequence number
sections.body: A SYN counts as one byte of sequence space, which is why the acknowledgment is ISN+1 (101 and 301 above).

A flood of SYNs fills the server's half-open queue. SYN cookies encode state in the server's ISN so no memory is held until the final ACK returns with a valid cookie, letting the connection be rebuilt.

subtopics.title: Simultaneous open
subtopics.summary: Both sides send SYN at once.

sections.body: Rare but required: each moves SYN-SENT -> SYN-RECEIVED on seeing the other's SYN and then to ESTABLISHED after the SYN+ACKs, using four segments.
A SYN to a closed port draws a RST, and the client sees 'connection refused'. A silent timeout instead means a firewall dropped the SYN.
TCP Fast Open lets data ride in the SYN on repeat connections. QUIC merges transport and TLS setup, needing one round trip (or zero on resumption).

takeaways: SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK synchronizes sequence numbers in both directions.
SYN consumes one sequence number; ACK = ISN + 1.
Options like MSS, window scale, and SACK are negotiated in the SYNs.
Randomized ISNs and SYN cookies defend against spoofing and floods.

references.label: RFC 4987: TCP SYN Flooding Attacks and Common Mitigations
RFC 7323: TCP Extensions for High Performance
